body: Field survey filed: #5931 (capability-provider research widening, per Drew's 2026-11-04 ruling) covers the current option space relevant to this issue in §6.4 — the capability-token field (UCAN 1.0, Biscuit 3.x, macaroons, IETF AAT draft): attenuate-only offline-verifiable delegation is a solved, multiply-implemented pattern; open question is encoding vs ID-native objects. It is an inventory, not a decision — the section ends with the open questions this design needs to answer.

**Wave-2 cross-link from the worlds prior-art pass ([#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955) program).**

New evidence for the delegation-encoding question: Spritely's **Brassica Chat** prototype (Nov 2025) demonstrates the four-layer composition in production-adjacent form — (1) object capabilities for online access, (2) actors/async messaging over OCapN, (3) CRDTs for eventually-consistent offline messaging, (4) **certificate capabilities (zcaps) for offline authorization via delegation chains** — explicitly contrasting with ACL-based local-first apps (https://www.spritely.institute/news/composing-capability-security-and-conflict-free-replicated-data-types.html). The zcap layer is a third data point beside UCAN/Biscuit for attenuable, offline-verifiable delegation: chains of signed certificates rather than tokens. Full survey: `workspace/scratch/worlds-capabilities-brief-2026-11-04/prior-art-research.md`, Cluster 7.

## Queue triage — task 10302

**Verdict:** #5900 remains OPEN; the all-state PR search found no PR for it. Parent design #5686 and the capability-provider field survey #5931 are both open. The existing survey comment on this issue explicitly says it is an option inventory, not a design decision. Current main is 2aefba02b48cc5d44799a52d1ce67a476cf79d9b.

**Existing foundation:** the ID capability design at doc/2026-10-09T09-59-07Z_design_attenuated_capabilities/ records scope attenuation, delegation, expiry/use limits and revocation; pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs contains the corresponding ledger machinery. That work does not settle provider-specific identity/scope, risk classes, or approval flows, so #5900 is not already done.

**Triage scope and order:**
1. Keep this ticket to provider grants: capability/provider/consumer binding, purpose and rate/volume bounds, expiry, issuance/approval by sensitivity, and the observation-versus-actuation distinction. Do not re-decide declaration, discovery, negotiation, or each target's transport; those are the parent and sibling tickets' scope.
2. Start from the parent #5686 authority/ceiling model and the existing ID grant/delegation machinery. Use #5931 as evidence, then make an explicit choice between ID-native grant objects and a token encoding (including rejected alternatives); the survey itself does not choose.
3. Specify attenuation, revocation, expiry/use limits and provider lifecycle; coordinate offline/cached-grant behavior with #5904 rather than duplicating its whole design.
4. Record invariants and alternatives in a linked doc/ decision record, then close this design ticket only when its acceptance criteria are met. Split only if the decision work identifies a genuinely independent design boundary.

**Blockers:** none to starting the design. The research input is already linked in the issue comments; its still-open status is not a dependency. No code changed in this triage.
